idea.title: Why a comet's tail points away from the Sun
idea.description: The tail is not a wake: what pushes it.

shots.visual: a comet moving away from the Sun, tail ahead
shots.narration: Comets are observed to move away from the Sun with the tail leading.
shots.shows: the tail leads the comet outward

shots.visual: the same stream reaching Earth, a city's lights going out
shots.narration: The cause of this orientation also reaches Earth. In March 1989 a storm in it put Quebec's power out for nine hours.
shots.shows: the stream that bends the tail arrives at Earth

shots.narration: The mechanism responsible is described below.
Sunlight exerts a small pressure, sufficient to move grains of dust.

shots.visual: a straight gas tail beside a curved dust tail
shots.narration: A comet also has a second tail, of gas, which is straight and fast. Its speed exceeds what sunlight alone can produce.
shots.shows: the gas tail outruns the dust tail

shots.visual: the two tails, the straight one highlighted
shots.narration: In 1951 Ludwig Biermann proposed that a further force was acting.

shots.visual: particles streaming out from the Sun past a comet
shots.narration: That force is a continuous outflow of particles from the Sun, emitted in every direction, all the time.
shots.shows: particles leaving the Sun and bending the gas tail

shots.narration: Eleven years later Mariner 2 flew through it and measured it. It is known as the solar wind.
The orientation of the comet is therefore explained.

shots.visual: the opening comet, the stream visible
shots.narration: The tail is oriented away from the Sun owing to the solar wind.
shots.shows: the tail pointing along the stream
